memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'or if they find lost property and lie about it, or if they swear falsely about any such sin that people may commit—'" - Lev 6:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the moment a mistake becomes something worse.

Someone finds lost property. That is not yet sin — anyone can find something. But then comes the choice: return it, or deny knowledge of it. And if challenged, swear an oath that they never saw it.

Notice the progression. First the keeping. Then the lie. Then the oath that drags God's name into the cover-up.

Sin rarely stays one size. It recruits. A small dishonesty needs a larger lie to protect it, and that lie needs another. Most people who end up badly compromised did not begin by choosing something enormous. They chose something small and then chose to defend it.

James describes the sequence: after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death (Jas 1:15).

The mercy is that the chain can be broken at any link. The person in this verse can still stop, still confess, still return what was found. It is harder now than it would have been at the start — but it is not too late.

Whatever you are currently protecting with a story: the shortest route out is the truth, today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I maintaining a story that requires more stories to hold it up?
2. What small thing could I put right today before it grows?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want to keep defending what I should simply confess. Give me the courage to tell the truth and stop the chain. Amen.
